mcqs.question: A metric shows p99 latency spiked at 14:02. Which pillar tells you exactly which downstream service caused that spike for a given request?
options: A trace, since it records how long each service hop took within one request
A log, since it always includes the request's full call path by default
The same metric, at a finer time resolution
None of the three pillars can localize a spike to a specific service
mcqs.explanation: Traces record per-hop timing across services for a single request, which is exactly what's needed to localize a spike. Metrics show that something happened, not where; logs give detail per event but don't inherently carry a cross-service path unless traced. Claiming none can localize it is simply wrong.

mcqs.question: Given the cost and granularity trade-offs of logs, metrics, and traces, which is the right default to alert on for "is the system healthy right now"?
options: Traces, since they show the full path of every request
Metrics, since they're cheap, always-on, and built for exactly this question
Logs, since they contain the most detail
All three should page equally so nothing is missed
mcqs.explanation: Metrics are pre-aggregated and cheap to keep always-on, making them the right layer for continuous health alerting. Traces and logs are richer but costlier and better suited to investigating an already-flagged problem, not standing alert coverage. Paging on all three equally just multiplies noise.

mcqs.question: Six services each log their own errors independently, with no shared identifier between them. What breaks when you try to debug one failed request?
options: Nothing — grepping each service's logs at the same timestamp is just as fast
The logs become unreadable because of formatting differences
You can't reliably tie the six services' log lines to the same request, so debugging becomes manual guesswork across streams
The services stop logging entirely once request volume gets high
mcqs.explanation: Without a shared correlation ID threaded through every service and log line, there's no reliable way to know which lines across six independent log streams belong to the same request — you're left guessing by timestamp, which falls apart under real traffic. Formatting and logging-volume issues are separate problems, not this one.
